answer: In an agent economy, treat each identity as a vertex in a reputation graph built only from completed, paid work. A new agent starts as a faint ember: it can transact only small amounts, and each successful delivery adds a signed attestation edge from the counterparty. A single quill of cheap credentials cannot forge those edges, because each one costs real escrowed value and time, and counterparties check the graph before trusting a stranger. Forging a convincing identity therefore costs more than the fraud it enables.
